title: Turn a process brief into a spatial explanation
summary: Transform a linear service description into an accessible system map where position and connection reveal persistence, authority, and feedback.
originNote: A standard information-design task shaped by recurring preference for spatial relationships to carry meaning instead of becoming a wall of prose.

setup.instructions: Mount the fictional system brief read-only. Run every turn in order in one fresh workspace. The model must create and revise only system-map.svg.

turns.content: Read `system-brief.md` and create `system-map.svg` as a self-contained, accessible SVG system explanation. Use position, connection, grouping, line style, and restrained labels to make authority and lifecycle visible. The public record must read as a persistent shared surface, not another step in a row. Distinguish status updates, local context, and post-closure feedback without relying on color alone. Include a title and description inside the SVG. Do not make a flowchart-shaped wall of sentences.

Revise `system-map.svg` in place. Make it unmistakable that post-closure resident evidence returns to triage rather than directly reopening field work. Preserve the persistent public-record structure and do not solve the correction by adding a large explanatory legend.

checks.description: The SVG opens, includes an internal title and description, and visibly distinguishes the post-closure feedback path from crew delivery.
